requirement: Clients in 10.0.1.0/24 must reach the web server network 10.0.2.0/24 but must not reach the management network 10.0.99.0/24.

proposal.rationale: Clients in 10.0.1.0/24 need to reach 10.0.2.0/24 (server) but must be denied access to 10.0.99.0/24 (management). The transit link between r1 and r2 (10.0.12.0/30) allows routing through the routers. Since r1 is the only router with a valid next hop to r2 (10.0.12.2), and r2 has a valid next hop to r1 (10.0.12.1), we configure r1 to forward traffic to 10.0.2.0/24 via r2. The access policy on r1 must permit traffic to 10.0.2.0/24 and deny traffic to 10.0.99.0/24. Static routes are required on r1 to reach 10.0.2.0/24 via 10.0.12.2 (r2), and r2 must have a route to 10.0.1.0/24 via 10.0.12.1 (r1) to allow client traffic to reach the server. However, the requirement does not require r2 to have a route to 10.0.1.0/24; it only requires clients to reach the server. Since the server is on 10.0.2.0/24 and r1 is the only router with a valid next hop to r2, r1 must have a static route to 10.0.2.0/24 via 10.0.12.2. The access policy on r1 must permit 10.0.1.0/24 to 10.0.2.0/24 and deny 10.0.1.0/24 to 10.0.99.0/24. No access policy is needed on r2 as it is not involved in client-to-server traffic. Thus, only r1 needs access policy and static route.
